propositions: Authorship ledger entries retain pre-rewrite commit SHAs after history rewrite, causing the verifier to misclassify authentic ledger entries when commit SHAs change but event positions and tree state remain valid.
The current verifier trusts stored commit SHAs unconditionally and only uses position-based resolution when commit SHA is null, failing to recover when a compacted ledger carries stale non-null SHAs.

History-rewrite regression proves that signed events with compacted ledger entries containing non-null pre-rewrite SHAs are misclassified as key-not-valid-at-era after commit history rewrite, despite event position and tree integrity remaining unchanged.

The verifier must resolve ledger position against current-history and prefer the newly resolved commit SHA over the stored pre-rewrite SHA, falling back to recorded SHA only when position resolution fails.
